options.D: Turn off the main breaker switch every time

explanation: Pulling on the cord itself damages the internal wires and can expose live metal, causing shocks or fires. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is a common barrier that nurses frequently encounter in community mental health care?

options.A: Too many available hospital beds in rural areas
options.B: Chronic funding shortages and cultural stigma
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of trained psychiatrists
options.D: Excessive community demand for group therapy

explanation: Lack of financial resources and social stigma against mental illness are major obstacles to providing effective community care. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h8)

question: In Nigeria, what color of bin liner is normally used for ordinary, non-hazardous general waste?

options.A: Brown
options.B: Black
options.C: Red
options.D: Yellow

explanation: Black bins and liners are standard for general municipal-type waste that carries no infectious risk. Easy to remember for your clinical rotations!

question: A nurse tests a new patient intake form and finds it saves time but needs two small tweaks. What should be done next?

options.A: Adapt the form with the needed tweaks and run another small test
options.B: Abandon all forms and return to chaotic verbal reporting forever
options.C: Punish the nurses for not making the original form perfect
options.D: Adopt the flawed form immediately across the entire national health system

explanation: Spot on! If an idea is almost there, we adapt it with our improvements and give it another quick test.

question: Why is using an AED as quickly as possible so important during cardiac arrest?

options.A: It automatically contacts the local police department for help
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying heart disease causing the arrest
options.C: It replaces the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.D: Survival rates drop significantly with every minute that defibrillation is delayed

explanation: Every single minute counts! Without blood flow, the brain quickly loses oxygen, so acting fast truly saves lives.

question: What happens when a hospital uses weak or outdated computer hardware for daily charting?

options.A: Enhanced security of confidential patient health records
options.B: System lag and workflow frustration for healthcare staff
options.C: Immediate conversion of the computer into a mainframe
options.D: Automatic upgrading of the device processor by the software

explanation: So true! Slow computers cause frustrating delays when you're trying to document care quickly and get back to your patients.

question: Why is it important for nurses to review immunization registers regularly?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salary and allowances
options.B: To identify children who have missed scheduled doses and need tracking
options.C: To find out which vaccine brand is most expensive
options.D: To report families to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Regular register checks help nurses spot missing children early so they can organize follow-up visits before outbreaks happen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: Why should a nurse in a public hospital care about civil service regulations?

options.A: It exempts the nurse from complying with the nursing and midwifery council acts
options.B: It allows the nurse to bypass hospital management during emergency procedures
options.C: It grants the nurse the authority to promote other junior staff members
options.D: It helps align clinical practice with administrative compliance and protects professional rights

explanation: Knowing your workplace rules helps you stay on the right side of management while protecting your rights on the job. You've got this!

question: A university student hides her pregnancy out of fear of expulsion and shame. What factor does this highlight?

options.A: A recognized legal indication for safe abortion
options.B: The direct physical effect of herbal toxins
options.C: Peer pressure and social stigma
options.D: Direct medical complication of hypertension

explanation: Fear of judgment and losing her education often pushes a student toward risky, secret procedures. Empathy from nurses is crucial!

question: How does setting small, realistic goals during follow-up visits help the patient?

options.A: It ensures the nurse does not have to do any paperwork
options.B: It replaces the need for any professional medical treatment
options.C: It builds their confidence and encourages active participation in recovery
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will never feel stressed again

explanation: Achievable goals empower patients, making them feel capable and involved in managing their own health. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: Who usually acts as the main bridge connecting the patient, family, and the rest of the medical team in home care?

options.A: The pharmaceutical manufacturer
options.B: The facility security guard
options.C: The home health nurse
options.D: The hospital billing clerk

explanation: That's you! Because you visit regularly, you naturally become the communication hub, keeping everyone updated on the patient's progress.

question: A patient has a viral cough and cold. Why won't standard antibiotics help clear it up?

options.A: Viruses multiply too slowly for antibiotics to catch them in time
options.B: Viral agents are too large to be penetrated by oral medications
options.C: Antibiotics immediately destroy the white blood cells fighting the virus
options.D: Viruses lack the cellular structures that standard antibacterial drugs target

explanation: Antibiotics are built to attack bacteria (like destroying their cell walls). Since viruses are structured differently, antibiotics just can't touch them!

question: What actually happens during the peer-review process before a study gets published in a journal?

options.A: The government checking the document for tax and financial compliance
options.B: Independent experts in the same field scrutinizing the manuscript for quality
options.C: The journal editor publishing the manuscript without any changes
options.D: Patients voting on whether they liked the treatment described

explanation: You got it! Other experts in the field carefully review the paper to make sure the science is solid before the public reads it.

question: A village thinks their stream water is fine, but lab tests show it is full of harmful bacteria. The nurse steps in to treat the water. What kind of need is this?

options.A: Normative need
options.B: Expressed need
options.C: Comparative need
options.D: Felt need

explanation: Even though the villagers didn't complain, professional testing uncovered the hidden danger. That expert-defined standard makes it a normative need!

question: Why do we give zinc supplements to a child with diarrhoea?

options.A: It acts as a strong sedative to help the child sleep
options.B: It shortens the illness duration and repairs gut tissue
options.C: It kills bacteria directly in the stomach lining
options.D: It immediately stops all vomiting within one hour

explanation: Zinc is a helper mineral! It helps the gut lining heal faster, boosts immunity, and cuts down how long the child will suffer from diarrhoea.

question: Which chemical element is found in proteins (amino acids) but is generally absent in pure carbs and fats?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Nitrogen
options.C: Phosphorus
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Spot on! Every amino acid contains a special amine group made of nitrogen, setting proteins apart from carbs and fats.

question: What is the heart of constructivist learning theory?

options.A: Behavior changes only occur through strict reward systems
options.B: Knowledge is an exact copy of what the textbook states
options.C: Learners actively build new knowledge using past experiences
options.D: Students learn best when they sit quietly and listen to lectures

explanation: You aren't just an empty bucket waiting to be filled! Constructivism means you connect new nursing concepts to what you already know from your own life and experiences.

question: What is the main difference between droplet and airborne germs?

options.A: Airborne germs only spread outdoors
options.B: Airborne germs cannot infect healthcare workers
options.C: Droplet germs need negative pressure rooms
options.D: Droplet germs travel on heavy particles that fall quickly, while airborne germs stay floating longer

explanation: Think of it by weight! Heavier droplets drop fast to the ground, but tiny airborne particles float around longer and need stronger masks.

question: A nurse opens a sterile dressing pack for a patient, but the procedure is cancelled before the pack is touched. What is the best nursing action to minimize waste?

options.A: Place the pack in the general waste bin to save space
options.B: Check hospital policy to see if the unopened sterile pack remains usable
options.C: Send the pack immediately to the hospital incinerator
options.D: Throw the unopened pack straight into the infectious waste bin

explanation: If a sterile barrier is completely intact and unopened, facility guidelines often allow it to remain sterile, preventing needless waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: Which condition is a primary indication for a low salt diet in hospital wards?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Acute bone fractures
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Hypertension is directly linked to sodium intake, making salt restriction a primary medical intervention for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: As a nurse giving injections in a clinic, up to what level should you fill your safety box before sealing it?

options.A: Only half full to save space
options.B: Packed tightly by pressing down with a hand
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: Filled completely to the absolute brim

explanation: Never overfill a sharps box! Sealing it when it's three-quarters full keeps everyone safe from accidental needle pricks.

question: What is the main goal of food fortification programs in public health?

options.A: Removing harmful chemical additives from local markets
options.B: Extending the shelf life of perishable meats
options.C: Adding essential nutrients to everyday foods to protect populations
options.D: Lowering the market cost of imported luxury foods

explanation: You got it! Fortifying common foods like salt or flour ensures that whole communities get key nutrients like iron and iodine without changing their daily habits.

question: Why do junior nurses often ask a veteran nurse for advice even though she has no official management title?

options.A: The veteran nurse holds formal authority over hospital scheduling.
options.B: The veteran nurse has legitimate power granted by the hospital board.
options.C: The veteran nurse holds strong expert power based on deep clinical experience.
options.D: The veteran nurse has coercive power to penalize poor performance.

explanation: Experience is everything! Expert power comes from deep knowledge and skills that naturally earn the respect of colleagues.

question: When is an asynchronous tele-nursing approach most useful?

options.A: When conducting a cardiac resuscitation emergency call
options.B: When sending recorded data or messages for a nurse to review later
options.C: When a patient is actively bleeding and needs immediate instructions
options.D: When performing a live physical examination over video

explanation: Think of asynchronous care as 'store-and-forward.' The patient sends a message or reading, and you check it when you have a moment.

question: As a community health nurse, you notice many toddlers are malnourished in a farming village. Which non-medical sector should you involve first?

options.A: Agriculture
options.B: Judiciary
options.C: Telecommunications
options.D: Transportation

explanation: Well done! Agriculture deals with food production and farming, making them our key partner in beating chronic malnutrition at its root.

question: What is the main goal of primary health care (PHC) services in Nigeria?

options.A: Handling complex surgical procedures for urban residents
options.B: Conducting advanced medical research in laboratories
options.C: Training international medical specialists
options.D: Bringing essential health services close to the grassroots

explanation: You've got this! Primary health care is all about bringing basic, friendly health services right down to the local communities where everyday people live.

question: Knowing the exact classification and drug-resistance profile of an infecting organism directly helps the nurse do what?

options.A: Determining the patient's expected hospital discharge date
options.B: Administering targeted antimicrobial therapy effectively
options.C: Calculating the patient's exact daily fluid intake
options.D: Choosing the correct hospital room wall paint color

explanation: When you know the exact bug and what drugs it hates, the medical team can prescribe the precise medication to knock it out quickly and safely.

question: Which action should a nurse take when conducting a mental health screening in a community clinic?

options.A: Build trusting rapport and explain the purpose of the screening questions
options.B: Diagnosing the patient with a psychiatric disorder immediately on the spot
options.C: Rushing through the questions so the patient does not feel uncomfortable
options.D: Ignoring non-verbal cues and focusing strictly on the written score

explanation: Establishing trust and explaining the purpose of screening helps reduce anxiety and encourages honest answers from the patient. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is a major risk of running a complete no-blame culture?

options.A: It increases the cost of buying hospital medical equipment
options.B: It completely stops communication between doctors and nurses
options.C: It fails to hold people accountable for reckless and dangerous actions
options.D: It guarantees that nurses lose their licenses right away

explanation: Total immunity can protect unsafe, reckless behavior. Balance is key to keeping patients safe!

question: What do we call the roles, behaviors, and expectations that society considers appropriate for men and women?

options.A: Physiological traits
options.B: Gender roles
options.C: Genetic mapping
options.D: Biological sex

explanation: Spot on! Gender roles are shaped by society and culture. Meanwhile, biological sex is strictly about your body's anatomy and genetics. You've got this!

question: A nurse is gently pressing on a patient's abdomen to check for tenderness and masses. Which physical examination technique is the nurse using?

options.A: Auscultation
options.B: Palpation
options.C: Inspection
options.D: Percussion

explanation: Palpation involves using the hands and fingers to feel parts of the body for tenderness, lumps, or abnormal size. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h2)

question: Why do patients with vulvitis often feel a burning sensation when passing urine?

options.A: The urethral opening becomes completely blocked by swelling.
options.B: Urine flows over raw, inflamed skin tissues on the vulva.
options.C: The kidneys produce acidic waste products that burn the bladder.
options.D: Urine mixes directly with digestive enzymes in the pelvis.

explanation: Imagine pouring liquid over a fresh scrape—when urine washes across sensitive, raw, or inflamed vulval skin, it naturally stings. Such a logical clinical connection to remember!

question: Which condition causes facial swelling, neck vein bulging, and trouble breathing due to a blocked major vein?

options.A: Spinal Cord Compression
options.B: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
options.C: Febrile Neutropenia
options.D: Tumor Lysis Syndrome

explanation: When a tumor presses on the superior vena cava, blood gets backed up in the upper body, causing that distinct facial swelling. Spotting this makes you a sharp nurse!

question: Why must nurses be careful when reading antibody blood tests for an active infection?

options.A: Antibodies only work when the patient has a high fever
options.B: Antibodies can stick around in the blood long after an old infection is gone
options.C: Antibodies change shape daily inside the human bloodstream
options.D: Antibodies destroy the laboratory testing equipment if left too long

explanation: Well done! Because our immune system remembers past fights, a positive antibody test might just mean an old infection, not a current one.

question: What is the primary purpose of a performance appraisal in nursing management?

options.A: To find reasons to terminate employee contracts immediately
options.B: To replace daily clinical supervision entirely
options.C: To evaluate job performance and guide professional growth
options.D: To decide which nurse gets the biggest office space

explanation: Appraisals measure work against standards to help staff improve their clinical practice and develop professionally. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABCDE systematic assessment approach?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Breathing
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Bleeding

explanation: In the ABCDE emergency assessment framework, B stands for evaluating the patient's breathing status and chest movement. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient wakes up abruptly and wants to walk to the bathroom. What should you do first?

options.A: Insist they use a bedpan instead of walking
options.B: Ask a family member to carry the patient
options.C: Help them stand up and walk very quickly
options.D: Have them sit on the bed edge for a moment

explanation: Allowing the patient to sit up slowly helps prevent sudden blood pressure drops that cause dizziness and falls. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h3)

question: Which day hospital setup shares resources directly with a larger general or psychiatric hospital?

options.A: The virtual outreach model
options.B: The mobile crisis model
options.C: The standalone model
options.D: The integrated model

explanation: Well done! The integrated model is physically and administratively linked to a main hospital, sharing staff and facilities.

question: You notice local food vendors leaving cooked rice uncovered in an open market stall. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Provide practical education on food protection and cover methods
options.B: Close down all food businesses in the region permanently
options.C: Imprison the vendors without warning or explanation
options.D: Ignore the practice since it is a traditional custom

explanation: Fantastic nursing judgment! As public health nurses, our first superpower is education. Always teach and guide before jumping to harsh punishments.

question: What is the main psychological feature of illness anxiety disorder (hypochondriasis)?

options.A: Complete lack of awareness regarding bodily changes
options.B: Intentional simulation of physical disease for attention
options.C: Frequent hallucinations involving internal organ failure
options.D: Excessive anxiety about having a serious illness

explanation: You've got this! The core thing to remember here is constant, overwhelming worry about having a severe medical condition, even when medical tests show everything is fine.

question: When must a nurse notify the police or a coroner about a patient's death?

options.A: When the family refuses to leave the room
options.B: When the exact cause of chronic illness is known
options.C: When the death is sudden or suspicious
options.D: When the patient dies during a weekend shift

explanation: Exactly! Any sudden, unexplained, or suspicious death needs to be reported to the authorities for a proper check.

question: A patient takes too much of an opioid pain medication and their breathing drops to just 4 breaths per minute. Why does this happen?

options.A: Cerebral cortex voluntarily suppressing the urge to breathe
options.B: Peripheral muscles failing to respond to normal nerve signals
options.C: Medullary respiratory centres suppressed by circulating drug molecules
options.D: Carotid baroreceptors shutting off blood flow to the lungs

explanation: Opioids can bind to the brainstem and quiet down the breathing center so much that it forgets to signal the body to breathe at a normal rate.

question: What usually happens shortly after a care-seeking patient gets normal test results from a doctor?

options.A: The anxiety returns and doubt creeps back in
options.B: The patient is permanently cured of all health fears
options.C: The patient stops visiting hospitals for the rest of life
options.D: The patient develops severe physical paralysis

explanation: Medical reassurance rarely lasts long for them. Soon enough, doubt creeps back in, and they start questioning if the lab results were a mistake.

question: Why must you always inspect the tip of an IV catheter after you remove it?

options.A: To determine what gauge size was used for the infusion
options.B: To measure the exact length of the vein inside the client's arm
options.C: To ensure the catheter tip broke off completely or remained intact
options.D: To check if any blood clots formed inside the plastic tubing

explanation: Always double-check that tiny plastic tip! Ensuring it's in one piece means no broken plastic fragment floated off into the patient's bloodstream.

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when talking to government policymakers?

options.A: To reduce the time spent in official meetings
options.B: To comply with international nursing trade laws
options.C: To make the message clear and easy to understand
options.D: To hide mistakes made during patient care procedures

explanation: Spot on! Policymakers aren't nurses. Using plain, simple language ensures they actually understand the issue and take action.

question: What is the very first thing you should do the moment an AED arrives?

options.A: Turn on the AED power
options.B: Check the patient for a carotid pulse
options.C: Deliver a manual shock immediately
options.D: Apply the adhesive pads to the chest

explanation: Just flip the power switch! The machine will start talking to you and guide you through every single step, making it super easy to follow.

question: What is the main class of drugs used to treat parasitic worm infections?

options.A: Anthelmintics
options.B: Antivirals
options.C: Antifungals
options.D: Antiseptics

explanation: You've got this! 'Anti' means against, and 'helmint' refers to worms. Anthelmintics are designed specifically to kick worms out of the body.

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the gut?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach while peristalsis is in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation mixes food back and forth rather than moving it forward.
options.C: Segmentation is controlled by the brain while peristalsis is automatic.
options.D: Segmentation stops all digestion while peristalsis speeds it up.

explanation: You're doing great! While peristalsis pushes food forward, segmentation uses ring-like squeezes to thoroughly blend food back and forth with digestive juices.

question: What is the purpose of an advance care directive in nursing practice?

options.A: To state a resident's medical treatment preferences before they lose decision-making capacity
options.B: To outline the daily cleaning schedule for the resident's private room
options.C: To mandate immediate emergency surgery for all sudden health crises
options.D: To authorize the nursing staff to make financial investments on behalf of the family

explanation: Correct! An advance directive lets patients clearly state what medical treatments they want or do not want before they become unable to decide.

question: An autistic patient gets very upset when you shift their routine by just ten minutes. What core feature does this reaction show?

options.A: An intentional attempt to disrupt the ward
options.B: A sign of sudden memory loss
options.C: A rigid adherence to routines and resistance to change
options.D: A lack of basic physical sensation

explanation: It's completely normal for them to feel unsettled here. Predictability brings comfort, so unexpected changes to routines can cause real anxiety.

question: What is the main benefit of encouraging nurses to report 'near misses' in the clinic?

options.A: It allows managers to calculate exact salary deductions for staff
options.B: It gives the hospital legal protection against malpractice lawsuits
options.C: It fulfills mandatory federal tax reporting requirements
options.D: It helps the unit fix system flaws before a real patient injury happens

explanation: Near misses act like early warning signs, giving the team a chance to fix hidden dangers before a patient gets hurt.

question: What is the general relationship between calcium and phosphate in our blood?

options.A: They always rise and fall together at the same time
options.B: They generally move in opposite directions
options.C: They both depend entirely on daily sodium intake
options.D: They have no chemical or physiological connection

explanation: Think of them like a seesaw! In the blood, when calcium goes up, phosphate usually goes down. You're doing great learning these dynamics.

question: During a sudden storm, a boat nurse needs to assess a patient. What is the most important first step for safety?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative so the patient sleeps through the storm.
options.B: Leave the patient unattended until the vessel reaches calm waters.
options.C: Transport the patient immediately to the captain's private quarters.
options.D: Secure the patient firmly against the ship's movement during the assessment.

explanation: Well done! Keeping the patient from falling or sliding as the ship rocks is always the top safety priority during rough weather.

question: Why is it so important to create a private, judgment-free space when screening a patient for abuse?

options.A: To stop the patient from asking questions about their drugs
options.B: To follow hospital billing rules for emergency room visits
options.C: To help the patient feel safe enough to share sensitive information
options.D: To make sure the doctor finishes the physical exam quickly

explanation: Exactly! Victims of violence often hide what happened out of fear or shame. Privacy and a warm, safe approach make all the difference.

question: Why should a nurse view medication administration protocols as a safety net?

options.A: They catch potential mistakes before the drug reaches the patient
options.B: They automatically calculate the correct drug dosage for the patient
options.C: They prove to the hospital management that the nurse is working hard
options.D: They prevent the pharmacy from ever making a dispensing mistake

explanation: Protocols act as multi-layered checks that intercept errors originating from prescribing, dispensing, or preparation stages. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h1)

question: When a nurse takes up a job in a government or private hospital, what is their legal relationship with the hospital?

options.A: A corporate executive with administrative immunity
options.B: An independent contractor with no hospital ties
options.C: A legal agent who owns the hospital facility
options.D: An employee bound by a contract of service

explanation: When you sign a contract to work in a health institution, you become an employee under a formal work agreement. You've got this!

question: What is a key duty of a nurse acting as a facilitator in a community?

options.A: Punishing community members who refuse to take their medications
options.B: Demanding immediate resignation of corrupt hospital directors
options.C: Writing new national health laws without community input
options.D: Connecting marginalized groups with health resources and social programs

explanation: Spot on! As a facilitator, your job is to bridge the gap—connecting people who need help with the exact services and agencies that can provide it.

question: What is the standard treatment to cure a benign primary heart tumour?

options.A: High-dose radiation therapy alone
options.B: Strict bed rest and fluid restriction
options.C: Surgical excision
options.D: Long-term oral antibiotic therapy

explanation: Since it's a physical mass, the best way to deal with a benign heart tumour is to surgically cut it out. Clean and effective!

question: A pot of cooked rice was left on the table for 5 hours on a warm afternoon. What should be done with it?

options.A: Place the rice straight into the freezer for future meals.
options.B: Reheat the rice thoroughly on the stove to kill all toxins.
options.C: Wash the rice with clean water before serving it again.
options.D: Discard the rice because it sat too long in the Danger Zone.

explanation: Leaving food out too long lets germs multiply and make toxins that heat cannot fix. When in doubt, throw it out to keep patients safe!

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of stress urinary incontinence after childbirth?

options.A: Passing large amounts of urine only at night
options.B: A constant burning sensation when passing urine
options.C: Leaking urine when coughing or sneezing
options.D: Inability to empty the bladder completely

explanation: You're doing great! Stress incontinence happens when sudden pressure (like a cough or sneeze) beats a tired, weakened pelvic floor.

question: Which muscle group is primarily activated by the femoral nerve?

options.A: Quadriceps femoris
options.B: Gastrocnemius
options.C: Gluteus maximus
options.D: Hamstrings

explanation: The femoral nerve innervates the quadriceps muscles on the front of the thigh, which are responsible for straightening the knee. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h7)

question: How does chronic viral hepatitis usually behave differently from acute hepatitis in the early stages?

options.A: Chronic infections often cause no symptoms for many years while silently damaging the liver
options.B: Chronic infections always start with a sudden, violent fever and severe vomiting
options.C: Chronic infections resolve completely within two to four weeks without any treatment
options.D: Chronic infections only affect older adults with pre-existing kidney disease

explanation: That's why chronic strains like Hepatitis B and C can be so tricky—they can hide out in the body for years without giving any warning signs!

question: During which stage of an infection does a patient first feel generally 'off' with vague, mild fatigue?

options.A: The convalescent stage
options.B: The illness stage
options.C: The prodromal stage
options.D: The incubation period

explanation: The prodromal stage is that tricky early window where a patient just feels mildly tired or has a low-grade fever before the main symptoms show up.

question: Which of these is an example of secondary data during a community assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions with village youths
options.B: Interviews conducted with mothers at the market
options.C: Existing clinic registers and census reports
options.D: Direct observation of village water sources

explanation: Correct! Secondary data is information that's already gathered and sitting there waiting for you, like old hospital records and government census books.

question: Which of the following practices represents a serious breach of patient data security?

options.A: Logging out of the electronic health record system after finishing a shift
options.B: Using a secure hospital database to check current medication guidelines
options.C: Posting a patient's clinical case details and photo on a personal social media page
options.D: Asking an IT technician for help fixing a broken network cable

explanation: Sharing identifiable patient information online violates patient privacy laws and breaches professional ethical standards. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h6)

question: In public health and nursing, what do the letters IEC stand for?

options.A: Investigation, Empowerment, and Cure
options.B: Immunization, Environment, and Control
options.C: Illness, Evaluation, and Care
options.D: Information, Education, and Communication

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication. You'll use these core tools every day in community health to spread awareness and help people stay healthy!

question: How does an RCA team usually investigate an adverse event?

options.A: Blaming the most junior nurse on duty during the shift
options.B: Asking successive layers of 'why' to find deep system weaknesses
options.C: Ignoring past incidents to focus only on the current patient
options.D: Throwing away all existing hospital safety manuals

explanation: By asking 'why' over and over, the team gets past the surface and uncovers the real workflow issues that caused the problem.

question: Why does dragging an inoculation loop in a zigzag pattern across an agar plate create isolated colonies?

options.A: It heats up the agar so the microbes melt into the gelatin
options.B: It spreads out the cells so individual ones land far enough apart to form separate mounds
options.C: It adds fresh nutrients to the edges of the plastic dish
options.D: It forces all the bacteria to sink deep down to the bottom of the Petri dish

explanation: You got it! Spreading the sample thins out the clustered cells, allowing single cells to grow into distinct, separate mounds.

question: A surgical instrument slips from your hand and lands partially on the edge of the instrument table tray. What should you do?

options.A: Consider the instrument contaminated and discard it immediately.
options.B: Wipe the instrument with an alcohol swab before using it again.
options.C: Inspect the instrument to see if it touched the floor.
options.D: Use the instrument quickly before air contaminants settle on it.

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! Touching that unsterile edge means the tool is no longer safe for the sterile field.

question: What is the main duty of NAFDAC regarding medications?

options.A: Providing free meals to hospitalized patients
options.B: Regulating drug manufacturing, importation, and quality
options.C: Issuing practicing licenses to individual bedside nurses
options.D: Managing the internal budget of teaching hospitals

explanation: NAFDAC ensures that all drugs sold or used in the country are safe, effective, and of good quality. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the current stance of global health organizations regarding a completely safe level of alcohol consumption?

options.A: Safe levels depend entirely on a person's physical height and weight
options.B: No level of alcohol consumption is considered entirely free of health risks
options.C: Only heavy spirits carry health risks, while wine and beer are completely safe
options.D: Consuming up to five drinks daily provides proven cardiovascular protection

explanation: Even though people enjoy a drink socially, health experts note that any amount of alcohol carries some degree of risk to the body, especially over time.

question: What is the main purpose of a variance report in nursing management?

options.A: To calculate individual nurse salaries and performance bonuses
options.B: To assess patient physical recovery rates after surgery
options.C: To determine which medical equipment manufacturers to sue
options.D: To compare budgeted financial targets with actual expenses

explanation: Variance reports show where financial goals were hit or missed, helping managers make smart adjustments for the future.

question: Where would you find the exact technical steps for managing a sterile surgical tray in the operating room?

options.A: In the general hospital-wide employee dress code policy
options.B: In the national labor law handbook for public workers
options.C: In the specialized departmental protocol for the theatre
options.D: In the hospital billing and revenue collection guide

explanation: Highly technical, unit-specific procedures live in departmental protocols rather than broad, general hospital rulebooks.

question: Which of the following is an example of resource tracking during a disaster?

options.A: Counting how many hours of sleep nurses got last night
options.B: Interviewing community leaders about past local floods
options.C: Predicting what the weather will look like next month
options.D: Monitoring available hospital beds and oxygen tank supplies

explanation: Resource tracking keeps an active count of vital physical items and space needed to care for incoming patients. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a primary source in nursing research?

options.A: A systematic review article written by an outside professor
options.B: A newspaper editorial commenting on a new health policy
options.C: A textbook chapter summarizing ten different research articles
options.D: An original research report written by the scientists who did the study

explanation: Primary sources are direct, firsthand accounts written straight by the actual researchers who performed the study.

question: What does the handy acronym IMRAD stand for in research writing?

options.A: Introduction, Management, Results, and Documentation
options.B: Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion
options.C: Investigation, Materials, Review, and Data
options.D: Information, Measurement, Reporting, and Analysis

explanation: IMRAD is just a simple roadmap researchers use to organize their papers. Once you know it, reading studies becomes super easy!

question: What type of data is best displayed using a bar chart?

options.A: Individual patient DNA sequences
options.B: Raw unorganized audio
options.C: Categorical data
options.D: Continuous time data

explanation: Bar charts are specifically designed to show and compare distinct groups or categories of information. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a positive feedback loop in the human body?

options.A: Parathyroid hormone halting when blood calcium levels normalize
options.B: Insulin stopping the release of glucose once blood sugar drops
options.C: Oxytocin release intensifying uterine contractions during childbirth
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH release when levels are high

explanation: Unlike negative feedback, positive feedback amplifies a signal! During labor, oxytocin makes contractions stronger, which releases even *more* oxytocin until the baby is born.

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, when does a critical incident or accident actually happen?

options.A: When holes in all defense layers align at the same time
options.B: When the hospital management changes all safety policies
options.C: When a single nurse makes a minor math calculation error
options.D: When a patient refuses to take prescribed medications

explanation: Brilliant! Accidents happen only when multiple safety barriers fail simultaneously, letting the error reach the patient. Keep pushing forward!

question: What ethical principle supports a patient's right to make their own choices about their care plan?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Negligence
options.C: Maleficence
options.D: Paternalism

explanation: Autonomy is all about self-determination—respecting the patient's right to understand their options and make decisions about their own body and treatment.

question: During antenatal clinic visits, which physical measurement is commonly used to track how the baby is growing?

options.A: Abdominal girth
options.B: Maternal weight gain
options.C: Pelvic diameter
options.D: Fundal height

explanation: Correct! Measuring the distance in centimeters from the pubic bone to the top of the uterus helps midwives and nurses check if the baby is growing right on track.

question: What do we call a live, real-time tele-nursing session?

options.A: Mailing written symptom diaries to the clinic
options.B: Automated tracking of vital signs overnight
options.C: Sending recorded messages for later review
options.D: Real-time interaction using live video or phone calls

explanation: Synchronous care is just like a live phone or video chat where you and the patient talk and respond to each other right away!

question: What is the main purpose of using a syringe driver in clinical practice?

options.A: To flush blocked intravenous lines rapidly with sterile saline
options.B: To deliver a continuous, controlled amount of medication
options.C: To provide intermittent bolus doses every five minutes
options.D: To measure precise hourly urine output in critical care

explanation: A syringe driver is specifically designed to infuse medications slowly and steadily over a set duration. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which of these options is NOT something a nurse needs to track after giving an antidote?

options.A: Daily shoe size and foot width measurements
options.B: Continuous vital signs and breathing patterns
options.C: Relevant laboratory markers and blood gas results
options.D: Neurological alertness and mental status

explanation: Your patient's shoe size won't tell you how they are recovering from poison! Breathing, alertness, and lab results are what truly matter.

question: Why can an overweight patient still suffer from malnutrition?

options.A: Excess body fat does not guarantee adequate vitamin and protein intake
options.B: Overweight patients are unable to absorb any nutrients
options.C: Lab tests cannot measure nutrition in larger bodies
options.D: Obesity completely stops the digestive tract from working

explanation: Malnutrition means poor nutrition, which includes lacking essential vitamins and minerals regardless of body weight. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h3)

question: Which vaccine is routinely administered to pregnant women during antenatal care visits to prevent a specific neonatal infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Bacille Calmette-Guérin

explanation: Pregnant women receive tetanus toxoid injections during antenatal visits to protect both mother and newborn against tetanus. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h4)

question: A resident says they already took their morning blood pressure pill, but the medication administration record (MAR) is blank for that time. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a second dose immediately to ensure their blood pressure stays controlled
options.B: Wait until the evening shift to see if the blood pressure spikes
options.C: Assume the resident is correct and sign the record as given by the resident
options.D: Withhold the dose and consult the prescribing physician or charge nurse before acting

explanation: Brilliant! Giving a double dose can be dangerous. Always pause, check the facts, and consult your senior colleagues or doctor when something doesn't match up.

question: Why does a nurse perform a head-to-toe examination instead of only checking the patient's main complaint?

options.A: To detect subtle changes and physical signs of illness across all body systems
options.B: To fulfill hospital administrative requirements without clinical benefit
options.C: To quickly discharge the patient from the ward without delay
options.D: To avoid having to ask the patient about their medical history

explanation: Looking at the whole person helps uncover hidden issues that might be related to, or worsened by, the main complaint. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)
